extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners (PRSA members), PR students, and other communications professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the structure and substantive elements of the PRSA Code of Ethics, describing its preamble, six professional values, six code provisions (with core principles, intents, guidelines, and improper-conduct examples), and a pledge to uphold the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble (aspirational orientation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preamble that sets out the goals and role of the document; describes the ethical orientation of PRSA and the desire for ethical behavior among members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the Code's aspirational nature. Notes that no formal enforcement system exists but PRSA may restrict membership for violations. Serves to frame the Code as guidance rather than a legalistic rulebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional value: Advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy is listed as one of six 'fundamental beliefs that guide our behaviors and decision-making process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy emphasizes the value of PR services to clients; it is meant to guide practitioners in promoting client interests ethically while balancing other values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional value: Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Honesty is listed as one of six 'fundamental beliefs that guide our behaviors and decision-making process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honesty serves to improve the reputation of the industry and is a core expectation for truthful communications and transparent practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional value: Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Expertise is listed as one of six 'fundamental beliefs that guide our behaviors and decision-making process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expertise signals the profession's commitment to competence and to improving the industry's reputation by delivering knowledgeable, skilled services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional value: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence is listed as one of six 'fundamental beliefs that guide our behaviors and decision-making process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence highlights the importance of objective judgment and freedom from improper influence when serving clients and the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional value: Loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Loyalty is listed as one of six 'fundamental beliefs that guide our behaviors and decision-making process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loyalty underscores the duty to serve clients and employers responsibly while balancing other professional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional value: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness is listed as one of six 'fundamental beliefs that guide our behaviors and decision-making process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fairness relates to equitable treatment of stakeholders and preserving the profession's reputation by avoiding deceptive or unjust practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code provisions of conduct (structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of six 'code provisions of conduct,' each elaborated with a core principle, 1–2 statements explaining the provision's intent, specific guidelines for behavior, and 2–4 examples of improper conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each provision follows a consistent structure: core principle (guiding statement), stated intent(s), 'A member shall' guidelines, and illustrative improper-conduct examples. This structure is used to apply the aspirational values to concrete professional behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision example: Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'competition' provision sets a core principle: 'promoting healthy and fair competition among professionals preserves an ethical climate while fostering a robust business environment.' Its stated intents include promoting respect and fair competition and serving the public interest by providing practitioner choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines under this provision include: 'A member shall follow ethical hiring practices designed to respect free and open competition without deliberately undermining a competitor' and 'A member shall preserve intellectual property rights in the marketplace.' Examples of improper conduct given: (1) an in-house member shares helpful information with a competing counseling firm during a competition for business; (2) a member spreads malicious/unfounded rumors about a competitor to alienate clients/employees as a ploy to recruit people and business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pledge to uphold the Code and accept sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the Code is a pledge to uphold the stated values and promote the profession's reputation, including acceptance of appropriate sanctions for aberrant behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pledge is an aspirational and symbolic commitment available for signature; although the Code lacks a formal enforcement mechanism, signing signifies a willingness to be held to the Code and to accept membership restrictions if violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of concrete improper-conduct examples for guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Across the six provisions, the Code provides 14 examples of improper conduct (2–4 examples per provision) to illustrate ethical breaches and guide practitioner judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examples are not exhaustive but are intended to provide concrete comparisons for professionals in questionable situations. They serve as practical anti-patterns that clarify how provisions apply in real-world contexts.
